gap: No result ChatGPT got states what Samsung's 45 W mode asks of the source in Samsung's own figures: its 45 W adapter (EP-T4510) offers PPS 3.3-11.0 V at 4.05 A, above the 3 A that the fixed 9 V / 15 V steps reach, and ships with a 5 A cable.
standout_why: Compared against Talk Android (no PPS, volt/amp lines, 5 A cable or two-device split; only 'Baseus lists PD, QC and Samsung Super Fast Charging support'), Pickstead (has a PPS table of 3-11 V at 2.72 A and a 24 W two-device total, but for the 30 W Anker A1259, not a 45 W bank), Anker's best-power-bank blog (only '45W max output when charging Samsung devices and 40W max for the iPhone 17 series') and Anker's own A1638 page, which is a cited result and already carries the 22.5 W split. So the split is not new; only the Samsung-side figures are. The part that would decide the pick, each bank's PPS amp ceiling, could not be read: us.ugreen.com, uk.ugreen.com, baseus.com and iniushop.com returned HTTP 429 on every attempt today. TechRadar's body came back truncated, and PopSci, PowerBankOnline, iTechGuides, Today, NYMag, Best Buy and the other uncited results were not opened.
decides: It does not yet change the pick. It sharpens ChatGPT's 'verify PPS' caveat into a test: for a Galaxy Ultra, a 45 W bank needs a PPS line above 3 A at about 10-11 V, and a built-in cable removes the 5 A cable question only if the bank publishes that line. Of the candidates, only Anker's A1638 was readable at the maker today: its spec lines top out at 3 A and show no PPS range, while its support article says Galaxy S and Z phones get up to 45 W over PPS. The UGREEN and Baseus PPS ranges are still unread at the maker; Notebookcheck and Best Batteries only say 'PPS' with no amps. Two side findings: Samsung's own pages do not state the page brief's '10 V / 4.5 A' figure, and Anker's A1638 was $45.99 today, not the $59.99 ChatGPT showed.
